title: Slow Database Queries
description: A pg_sleep() is injected before every DB operation, simulating a missing index, lock contention, or an overloaded Postgres instance.

true_root_cause.summary: DB layer is slow (db_slow=true, db_slow_seconds=2.0) — every query takes ≥2 s, causing high p95 latency across all endpoints

key_evidence_signals.expected_behaviour: p95 jumps to ≥2 s for every operation and endpoint
p95 rises to ≥2 s across all endpoints (GET and POST)
Throughput drops as each request blocks for 2+ seconds
Remains near zero — slow queries do not cause 500 errors
Ratio unchanged — same number of queries, they are just slower

red_herrings: High latency could suggest an N+1 bug — but query-count ratio is stable
Timeout errors may appear in Loki logs — these are a consequence, not the cause
recommended_fix: Identify and add missing index; or resolve lock contention; or scale Postgres
evaluation_checks: Agent identifies db_slow as the active flag
Agent cites db_query_duration_seconds p95 as primary evidence
Agent confirms error rate is stable (rules out error_spike)
Agent confirms query-count ratio is stable (rules out N+1)
